cases.note: A record that expires on nothing is valid and says nothing was checked — which is how a console tells "still valid" from "nobody set a policy".
Joint zeros drift with travel, not with the calendar (§45.2).

cases.note: F/T bias drifts with temperature continuously, so the delta is the rule and the direction does not matter.

cases.note: The rule that keeps an expiry policy from switching itself off: a robot whose temperature sensor has failed is precisely the robot whose bias should not be trusted.
cases.expected: {"records":[{"checked":[],"detail":"this record expires with temperature and no reading is available, so how far this robot has drifted from its calibration conditions cannot be established","guards":["envelope"],"reason":"temperature","set":"force_torque_bias","state":"expired"}],"unavailable":[{"detail":"the `force_torque_bias` calibration is expired — this record expires with temperature and no reading is available, so how far this robot has drifted from its calibration conditions cannot be established","guard":"envelope","set":"force_torque_bias","state":"expired"}]}

cases.note: The other boundary. Measured 3,600 s ago against a validity of exactly 3,600 s: still valid, and the checked list says so. Every age case was well inside or well outside, so `>` versus `>=` was free — and on a fleet recalibrating on a schedule, the two disagree about every robot on the day its policy comes due.

Half a second, rendered. `toFixed` takes the larger on a tie and Python’s formatting rounds to even, so this age is `3601` in one reading and `3600` in the other — in a sentence an operator reads and a corpus compares byte for byte. Nothing else in this corpus lands on a half.

The direction `temperature-delta`’s note claims does not matter, and which no case tested: every temperature case ran warmer than the calibration. An edition without the absolute value reads −18 °C as comfortably inside a 5 °C budget, so a bias measured in a heated cell and used in a cold store is trusted exactly where it drifts most.

cases.note: A record that expires with time and cannot say when it was taken. §45’s rule is that a missing reading never extends validity — the alternative is a policy that switches itself off on the record least able to account for itself. `temperature-unreadable` pins this for the *current* reading; nothing pinned it for the *taken* one.
